items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says 'the left boundary is clamped' but defines Gamma_D = {0}x(-0.5,0.5). That is the vertical mid-line of the stated domain (-1,1)x(-0.5,0.5), not the left edge x = -1. Several things favour x = -1: the 3D cantilever ({-1}x...), the eigenvalue case (g), and the Table 3 compliance (about 0.6). A mid-line clamp would leave the left half unloaded, the optimizer would fill the right half solid, and the compliance would be much smaller. Fig. 4, which would settle this, is not available. Only a (0,1)x(-0.5,0.5) domain would put both Gamma_D and Gamma_N on the edges, and that contradicts the stated domain and the 120x60 and 200x100 grids.
readings: Fully clamp (u_x = u_y = 0) the whole left edge x = -1 (x/L = 0), -0.5 < y < 0.5
Fully clamp the interior vertical line x = 0 (x/L = 0.5, mid-length), -0.5 < y < 0.5, leaving the left half of the domain unloaded

items.entity: downward load at centre of right edge (Gamma_N)
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 calls it a 'point load' but defines it as a traction t = (0,-1) on the segment Gamma_N = {1}x(-0.05,0.05), the central 10% of the edge height. The text does not settle whether to apply a single nodal force or a uniformly distributed edge traction. The segment spans about 6 elements on a 120x60 grid and 10 on a 200x100 grid.
readings: Uniform traction on x = 1 over -0.05 < y < 0.05 (y/H from 0.45 to 0.55, measured from the bottom edge)
Single concentrated nodal force at (1, 0), i.e. y/H = 0.5 on the right edge

items.entity: downward load at centre of right edge (Gamma_N)
items.description: t = (0,-1) is a traction density (Eqs. 3.16-3.17) on a segment 0.1 long, so the total force is 0.1. Calling it a 'point load' suggests a unit force instead. The two readings change the compliance by a factor of 100. Table 3 (J = 0.5953 APF-FNN, 0.6930 FEM-PF, with E = 1) matches a total force of about 0.1. Caveat: if the Ginzburg-Landau term with absolute weight gamma = 0.01, or the absolute volume-penalty weights, are reproduced, a 100x larger compliance acts like gamma = 1e-4 (see Fig. 9(iv)). In that case the layout would also change.
readings: Traction density 1 per unit length on the 0.1-long segment, total downward force 0.1
Total downward force 1 (unit point load, or traction density 10 on the segment)

items.entity: 2D constitutive assumption (plane stress vs plane strain) and thickness
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 gives only E = 1 and nu = 0.3. Sec. 3.2.1 writes C0 with the 3D Lame constant lambda = E*nu/((1+nu)(1-2nu)). Used in 2D, that formula means plane strain, whereas grid-based TO codes usually assume plane stress. Neither option is stated. The out-of-plane thickness is never given; the 2D integrals imply unit thickness. Plane strain is equivalent to plane stress with nu_eff = 0.43 and E_eff = 1.10. So the choice changes the compliance by about 10% and can change the layout slightly.
readings: Plane stress, unit thickness (lambda* = E*nu/(1-nu^2) = 0.330, mu = 0.385)
Plane strain per unit depth (lambda = 0.577, mu = 0.385), the literal Sec. 3.2.1 formula

items.entity: analysis/design grid resolution and element type
items.description: The APF-FNN run does not use a mesh. Sec. 4.1.2 gives only 2x10^4 interior points 'on a tensor-product grid'; Sec. 4.1.4 implies this is a 200x100 grid for the reported J = 0.5953. The FEM-PF comparison in Sec. 4.1.3 is said to use the identical setup, but on a '120x60 mesh' whose element type is not given (the FEniCS default is triangles). Because epsilon = 0.01 is fixed in physical units, the grid resolution matters; the sampling study shows J changing with point density.
readings: 120 x 60 square bilinear elements, h = 1/60 (FEM-PF baseline resolution)
200 x 100 square elements, h = 0.01 (matches the collocation grid of the reported APF-FNN result)
120 x 60 cells, each split into two linear triangles (FEniCS-style RectangleMesh)

items.entity: design regularization / minimum length scale (filter equivalent)
items.description: The paper uses no density or sensitivity filter. Regularization comes from two sources. One is the Ginzburg-Landau term (epsilon = gamma = 0.01, Sec. 4.1.1), added with absolute weight to the compliance. The other is the built-in frequency limit of the Fourier topology network (12x12 modes, omega_max_phi = 30, smallest feature about pi/30 = 0.1). No filter type, radius, or equivalent minimum length scale is given for an element-density solver. The Adam update of network weights also has no grid counterpart.
readings: Add gamma*Int(eps/2*|grad phi|^2 + 0.25*phi^2*(1-phi)^2/eps) with eps = gamma = 0.01 to the compliance on the grid, no filter
Density filter (optionally with projection) of radius about 0.05 (about 3 elements at h = 1/60), matching the ~0.1 minimum feature of the frequency-limited field
Conventional sensitivity or density filter of radius 1.5-2 elements

items.entity: Fourier bandwidths for case (a): omega_max_phi (topology) and omega_max_u (state)
items.description: Table 2 and Sec. 4.1.2 give omega_max_phi = 30 and omega_max_u = 35 for case (a). Sec. 4.1.4 gives the 'reference setting of case (a)' as omega_max_phi = 35 and omega_max_u = 30, and the Fig. 13 caption labels are garbled ('phase-field and toplogy networks'). Per Fig. 13, the phase-field bandwidth controls how much fine detail the design has, so it affects the length scale to emulate.
readings: omega_max_phi = 30, omega_max_u = 35 (Table 2 / Sec. 4.1.2)
omega_max_phi = 35, omega_max_u = 30 (Sec. 4.1.4)

items.description: beta = 0.5 is enforced only through a quadratic penalty (Eq. 3.18). Its starting value is given only as 'O(1)' (Sec. 4.1.2); unlike Tables 5-7, Table 2 does not list lambda_penal^(0). The penalty is divided by zeta = 0.98 each outer iteration and is said to reach 'O(10^3-10^4)'. Starting from 1, it would be 2.4x10^4 after 500 iterations. So the optimization path and the exact final volume are not uniquely defined.
readings: lambda_penal^(0) = 1, multiplied by 1/0.98 per outer iteration (about 2.4e4 at n = 500)
lambda_penal^(0) = 0.1, multiplied by 1/0.98 (about 2.4e3 at n = 500, inside the stated range)
No penalty: enforce mean density = 0.5 as a hard constraint (OC/MMA)

items.description: Sec. 4.1.3 gives only the 120x60 mesh, 100 outer x 20 inner iterations, and a pointer to the semi-implicit scheme of ref. [21]. It also cites a 'Section 2.3' that does not exist. Not given: the pseudo-time step or mobility, the element order, and how the volume constraint was handled (penalty values or Lagrange multiplier) in the run that produced J = 0.6930.
readings: Semi-implicit Allen-Cahn steps with dt = 1e-3 and the same quadratic volume-penalty schedule (lambda0 = 1, x1/0.98)
Same scheme with dt = 1e-2 and a Lagrange-multiplier volume correction at each inner step
OC/MMA on element densities with the Ginzburg-Landau term added to the objective (no pseudo-time evolution)
